On a Compose service the keep-alive lands on `entrypoint` rather than `cmd`: the reference overrides the service entrypoint with its own keep-alive wrapper, deacon leaves the entrypoint unset and lets the service's own command hold the container open. The same characterized difference as the single-container `cmd` tolerance, on the field Compose puts it in; `cmd` is compared here and agrees.

The Feature layer forces each CLI to build the service image itself, so Compose's label records a different content digest on each side (deacon `sha256:2badca10…`, reference `sha256:35612053…`, measured at oracle 0.87.0). A digest of two independent builds cannot agree; what the image CONTAINS is compared by `env`, `user`, `workingDir` and the mount graph on this same channel. The sibling sidecar case runs its service image unmodified and this label agrees there.
The keep-alive command strings differ; the observable behavior is measured equal (`docker stop` in ~200 ms, exit 0, on both). Scoped to `cmd`; every other field stays compared.

records.notes: Ports `parity_state_diff::compose-parity-with-feature-mount-gap` (res-cross-cli-state-snapshot). A Compose service plus a local Feature that contributes BOTH a `containerEnv` value and a bind mount — the combination behind #272, where deacon's compose path dropped Feature-contributed mounts that its single-container path applied. The legacy unit asserted the two facts by hand (`FEATURE_ENV_CONTROL` present as a positive control, `/feat-mnt` present on both sides) and then diffed the snapshots; this compares the whole normalized container state between the CLIs, so the mount graph, the env, the user and the network are all compared rather than two hand-picked keys. The legacy fixture's Feature mount was a NAMED VOLUME (`feat-probe-vol`) that the unit removed by hand; this fixture uses a workspace-relative bind instead — the claim is that a Feature-contributed mount reaches the service, not which type it is, and a fixed global volume name would collide between concurrent docker-shared cases and outlive whichever ran last. `labels.devcontainer.metadata` is deliberately NOT tolerated: deacon records mount sources with `${localWorkspaceFolder}` substituted away to the empty string on the compose path (`/sib` where the reference records `${localWorkspaceFolder}/sib`), which is a regression of #373 filed as #437, so this case reports it until the fix lands. Images pinned to debian:bookworm-slim (V18).

records.notes: Ports `parity_state_diff::compose-sidecar-and-named-volume` (res-cross-cli-state-snapshot). A two-service Compose project — the devcontainer service plus a sidecar neither CLI is told about — with a Compose-declared named volume on the primary service. Two claims the single-service compose cases cannot make: the sidecar's presence does not change which container is treated as the devcontainer (both sides inspect the `app` service and agree on its whole state), and a volume declared by COMPOSE rather than by devcontainer.json reaches the container identically. The legacy unit checked the volume with a hand-written type test on one mount destination; this compares the whole mount graph, so a sidecar-induced mis-selection shows up as wholesale disagreement rather than passing a single-key probe. `mountSources./data` is tolerated because a Compose volume's real name carries the project prefix, which is the already-characterized project-name difference; the project-relative name in `composeProjectResources.volumes` stays compared. Unlike the sibling feature-mount case, this service image is used UNMODIFIED, so `com.docker.compose.image` agrees here and is not tolerated — which is what keeps that tolerance honest over there. Images pinned to debian:bookworm-slim (V18).

records.notes: Ports `parity_state_diff::default-workspace-mount-target-parity` (res-cross-cli-state-snapshot). The config sets `workspaceFolder` and authors NO `workspaceMount`, so the mount TARGET is whatever each CLI defaults to — the divergence #273 closed, where deacon mounted the workspace at `workspaceFolder` (`/workspace`) instead of the spec default `/workspaces/<basename>`. The legacy unit encoded that as four hand-written assertions over the mount map (`/workspace` absent on each side, something bind-mounted under `/workspaces/` on each side); here it is ordinary equality of the whole normalized mount graph, which the `workspace_basename_token` rule makes comparable across the two sides' differently-named temp workspaces. A regression of #273 moves the bind to a different destination key and the comparison fails on it directly. Image pinned to debian:bookworm-slim (V18).

records.notes: Records the container-label surface both CLIs produce (024 Phase 5). Only the five deacon-only keys are excused; `local_folder`/`config_file` differ only by each side's own isolated temp workspace and are normalized by the workspace path token, so they must compare equal. This case's first live run reported `diverge` on two further paths — `labels.devcontainer.metadata` and `cmd` — and BOTH were fixed in deacon rather than tolerated (the cmd one was a 10s `docker stop` stall). They are now compared and must agree; no tolerance was added for either.

Faithful destination for parity_observable_state::container-and-image-labels (024 Phase 5). The legacy test runs DEACON ONLY — it never invokes the oracle — and asserts four facts about deacon's own container labels, so a spec-expectation is its honest shape; a live-differential would silently claim cross-CLI agreement the unit never checked. Two corrections to the baseline record, which overstated it: the unit declares chan-image but inspects no image at all (only Config.Labels of the container), and its assertion text says "and image" for the same reason. The hash-valued labels (configHash, workspaceHash) are deliberately NOT pinned to literals here — they are derived from the workspace path, which differs per run; the sibling live-differential case covers them by comparison. Distinguished from that sibling by oracle type. Image pinned to debian:bookworm-slim (V18).
